supersedes: modern/spec/pic2d/pic2d-model-v1.4.json (all v1.4 physics, gates, time step, checkpoint and artifact contracts are kept and apply over the whole domain; this file adds the optional plume block: L-shaped domain, internal channel walls, far-field boundary, cathode emission region, two-zone neutrals, momentum/thrust ledgers, plume diagnostics and the plume-boundary gate; a channel-only configuration is bit-identical to v1.4)
source_of_the_changes: modern/docs/literature/pic-mcc-blockers.md: blocker 4d (section 4.4 exit-plane / cathode boundary: Szabo 2001; Charoy et al. 2019; Boeuf and Garrigues 2018; Brandt et al. 2016; Duras et al. 2017; Matyash et al. 2010), blocker 3 (neutrals: Szabo 2001/2014; Brandt et al. 2016), 4.1 (ion-neutral: Miller et al. 2002 - deferred), blocker 6 (validation observables: Koch et al. IEPC-2011-236; Keller et al. 2015; Brandt et al. 2016)
what_changed: domain: optional plume box appended to the channel; the channel walls, the divergent cone and the exit lip become internal masked boundaries; the thruster front face is split into a dielectric flange and a grounded conductor; the far-field box boundary is Dirichlet at the reference potential
cathode: electron emission region (annulus in the plume) with fixed-current or current-continuity rule replaces the exit-plane injection (kept as the legacy option)
neutrals: two-zone closure - channel 0-D inventory (v1.4 with recycling; front-face ions not recycled) + analytic free-molecular cone in the plume as the local MCC factor

diagnostics: axial momentum ledger per interval (round-off closure), momentum-flux thrust per species + cold gas, momentum-balance thrust, Maxwell-stress force on every solid boundary, closure fraction; far-field histograms j_i(theta) and IEDF; exit-plane potential and acceleration region; Isp and anode efficiency

gates: peak-node Debye gate and grid-heating triad over the whole domain; plume-boundary charge pile-up gate (fail-closed); Poisson manufactured-solution and second-order truncation tests on the L-shaped mesh; force-balance (Newton's third law) test
field: direct P2 node evaluation over the plume box (spec/pic2d/p2-field-plume-extension-v1.json); the channel authority and all v1.x field identities are untouched

gates v2.0.3 (2026-09-04, after attempt 8): peak-node Debye gate in window mode (interval-averaged peak over the 400000-step window, hard pi = the CIC threshold, soft 2.5 = the resolution margin as a plateau precondition; single-step sample kept as witness) and a one-sided windowed residual-power gate (trailing-window ledger residual >= 5 % of the electrode work stops the run; the cumulative ratio demoted to a witness) - see gates_v2_0.peak_debye_gate_v2_0_3 / windowed_energy_residual_gate_v2_0_3 / gate_recalibration_history_v2_0_3

performance v2.0.5 (2026-09-04, audit recommendations 1 and 2 of docs/pic2d-performance-audit.md): born-ledger tallies folded into the MCC kernel and the born deposits into the spawn (no strided sums / single-thread adds in the step), the window-diagnostic branch forked onto a second CUDA stream inside the captured step, and an optional electron-moment sampling interval K (numerics.performance.moment_sample_interval; K = 1 default keeps every v2.0.x identity, K != 1 enters config_sha256) - physics bitwise, two ledger scalars at round-off; see performance_v2_0_5

geometry_keys.plume_radius_m: R_plume: outer radius of the box (far-field cylinder r = R_plume for z >= L_channel)
geometry_keys.body_dielectric_radius_m: r_body: the front face z = L_channel is dielectric (surface charge) for r_exit < r <= r_body and a grounded conductor for r > r_body

domain_v2_0.grid_rules: uniform (dr, dz) over the whole box (no graded spacing in the solver); the exit plane, the lip radius and r_body must lie on grid lines (Grid2D validation)
domain_v2_0.plasma_region: L-shaped: channel cells r < r_wall(z) for z < L_channel (one-cell stair-step cone) plus every cell of the plume box

boundaries.anode: z = 0, r < r_bore: Dirichlet U_a (absorbing conductor)
boundaries.channel_wall_and_cone: internal dielectric: masked solid nodes, plasma-side boundary nodes carry the accumulated surface charge; zero field inside (homogeneous Neumann, v1.x closure)
boundaries.front_face_dielectric: z = L_channel, r_exit < r <= r_body: internal dielectric ring with surface charge (the BN flange and, in divergent-exit-stack, the 4.0-4.4 mm gap in front of the pole stack closed as dielectric)
boundaries.front_face_conductor: z = L_channel, r > r_body: Dirichlet at the reference potential (exit_v). DECLARED grounded conductor: the soft-iron pole faces / shield of a HEMP-T are metal on the cathode/chamber reference (Kornfeld, Koch and Harmann 2007; Koch et al. 2011); a floating face would need a charge-balance closure with its own time scale
boundaries.far_field: r = R_plume (z >= L_channel) and z = z_max: Dirichlet exit_v (0 V chamber / neutraliser reference), the literature's practice (Brandt et al. 2016: 0 V Dirichlet on the outer boundaries; Matyash et al. 2010); switching to Neumann changed Brandt's plume current ratios, so the choice is declared and the pile-up gate checks it

domain_v2_0.particle_boundary_classes: anode, wall (channel dielectric incl. cone), body_face (front-face dielectric and conductor, tallied per species), exit (= far field in the plume geometry; the beam), invalid (Courant violation)
domain_v2_0.development_size: divergent-exit-stack: R_plume = 12 mm (4 r_exit, 6 r_bore; the return-yoke radius), L_plume = 12 mm (0.5 L_channel, BOUNDED by the P2 FEM domain z <= 36.25 mm - the 1-1.5 L_channel first size is deferred to a new FEM solve), uniform 50 um: 240 x 720 cells, 77,940 plasma cells, 78,228 unknowns; Brandt et al. 2016 comparison: 20 x 5 mm box behind a 14 x 1.5 mm channel (1.4 L x 3.3 r) 'still too small' for plume ratios
domain_v2_0.cost: measured 2026-09-03 (RTX 5090, CUDA-graph step): field map 6 s; host Schur factorisation of 241 axial-row blocks (721 x 721) ~5 min per launch, 1.0 GB on device; 4.2 ms/step at 0.55 M particles (direct-solve floor ~3 ms from 482 sequential row-block matvecs); projected 5-7 ms/step at 4-6 M particles

cathode_v2_0.class: CathodeConfig(r_inner_m, r_outer_m, z_start_m, z_end_m, electron_temperature_ev, current_a, current_rule, max_current_a, continuity_relaxation_intervals)
cathode_v2_0.emission: electrons born uniformly in the annulus volume (r^2-uniform, z-uniform) with an isotropic Maxwellian at electron_temperature_ev (the v1.x 2 eV); the Poisson step sees them at the next deposit; born momentum tallied (pz_injected)
cathode_v2_0.position: INSIDE the channel's exit flux tube in the plume (development run attempt 4: r 0.5-2.0 mm, z = L_channel + 0.3-1.0 mm). The first placement - an off-axis annulus in front of the pole face (attempt 3: r 4.5-6.0 mm = 1.5-2 r_exit, z = L_channel + 2-4 mm, the HEMP-T neutraliser position of Kornfeld, Koch and Harmann 2007 / Koch et al. 2011) - did not ignite: event-aware field-line tracing (cft_revival.pic2d.fieldlines, RK2 on the bilinear node field, terminations channel / anode / wall / body / far_field / axis / null) showed the channel's flux tube closes on the front face within ~1.5 mm of the exit (axis null at z = 25.45 mm) and that the annulus sat on pole-face-to-far-field lines (connected fraction 0/24); 95 % of the emitted current left through the far field, I_d -> 0, S fell x15 in 1.1 us. In an electrostatic model without anomalous transport and with a near-collisionless plume, electrons do not cross between flux tubes, so the emission region must lie on lines that enter the bore; it represents the arrival of the neutraliser electrons into the channel-connected tube (the real device crosses the weak-field region by collisions/instabilities the model excludes; Brandt et al. 2016 fed electrons from the far outer boundary at 1 eV in a model with Bohm transport). Declared, fail-closed: cathode.require_channel_connected_fraction (the runner re-traces the region at launch and records the result in summary.json cathode_connectivity)
cathode_v2_0.ignition_gate: stopping_rule.ignition_gate: trailing-window means of S and N_e at declared check times over their reference means after the seed dump (0.05-0.2 us); stop_reason no_ignition (fail-closed) when a check fails; calibrated on v1.3 attempts 1 (failed) / 2 (ignited) and plume attempt 3 - see the protocol note; the contingency if attempt 4 still fails is a declared ignition sequence (exit-plane injection inside the channel for the first N us ramped to zero while the plume cathode carries the current; switch time recorded and excluded from the plateau window), NOT implemented yet

rules.fixed: current_a every step (the v1.x fixed-current rule moved into the plume)
rules.continuity: the emitted current follows the previous series interval's discharge current I_d = e (anode electrons - anode ions)/interval, relaxed by an exponential moving average over continuity_relaxation_intervals intervals and clamped to [current_a (floor = ignition current), max_current_a]; charge conservation of the plasma gives I_cathode = I_d + (I_e - I_i)_far, so in steady state the far-field boundary carries no net current to the chamber. Review section 4.4 variant (c) (Szabo 2001 'injected at a rate which preserved quasineutrality'; Charoy et al. 2019 / Boeuf and Garrigues 2018 cathode-plane injection tied to the current leaving)

cathode_v2_0.legacy: InjectionConfig (exit-plane flux-weighted half-Maxwellian at fixed current) is kept for A/B; a config may carry a cathode or an injection, not both; the cathode requires a plume geometry
cathode_v2_0.recorded: currents_a.cathode_emission_a; momentum.cathode_target_rate_per_step / cathode_rate_per_step / cathode_emission_next_a / cathode_clamped; the live rate is checkpointed in cumulative[cathode_rate_per_step]

neutrals_v2_0.channel_zone: v1.4 0-D inventory over the CHANNEL plasma cells only (volume = channel_volume_m3): feed, exit-aperture effusion, ionisation (channel + plume ionisations both consume channel atoms: the plume atoms are the effused channel atoms), wall/anode ion recycling; ions absorbed on the front face are NOT recycled into the channel (they recombine outside)
neutrals_v2_0.plume_zone: n_g(r,z) = n_g,channel x f(r,z) with f the cosine-law point-source expansion of the channel's effusion flux Phi = n_g v_bar A_exit / 4 from the aperture centre: flux density Phi cos(theta) / (pi rho^2) at distance rho and polar angle theta, divided by the mean speed 3 pi v_bar / 8 of the effusing atoms, gives f = 2 A_exit cos(theta) / (3 pi^2 rho^2), capped at 0.5 (the outgoing half-Maxwellian at the aperture); f = 1 in the channel (free-molecular effusion through an orifice: Bird 1994). Used ONLY as the per-particle MCC probability factor (density_shape) in the null-collision scheme; the plume atoms are not an inventory of their own
neutrals_v2_0.null_collision_ceiling: the MCC null-collision ceiling carries declared headroom above the zero-ionisation density Q/c and the inventory starts at the declared initial_density_per_m3 (= Q/c): with recycling and the artificial relaxation, n_g tracks the rate-based fixed point (Q + R - S)/c, which exceeds Q/c while a seeded ion population drains (R > S) - the plume development run's first launch stopped fail-closed on this at 14 ns with the ceiling AT Q/c. In steady state R <= S bounds n* <= Q/c; the transient is an artefact of the development relaxation and is recorded (max n_g / (Q/c)). The real collision rate is unchanged (probability scale n_g / ceiling); the null-collision cost grows with the headroom (2x: 1.3e-4 per step)
neutrals_v2_0.relaxation_suspension: the artificial relaxation toward n* = (Q + R - S)/c is defined only while a fixed point exists; in any interval with S > Q + R (n* < 0) it is suspended and the inventory follows the conservative balance dn/dt = (Q + R - S - c n)/V alone (NeutralAdvance.artificial_relaxation_suspended; a guard, the v1.3/v1.4 channel runs never reached S > Q + R so their closure is bit-identical). tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_neutral_inventory.py::test_v20_artificial_relaxation_is_suspended_when_ionisation_exceeds_the_sources
neutrals_v2_0.graph_safe_mcc_density: DEFECT FIXED 2026-09-04 (plume attempts 4-5): the v1.4 CUDA-graph step passed the instantaneous MCC neutral density n_g0 x scale as a kernel scalar, which a captured graph freezes at capture time; the MCC therefore ionised at the n_g of the last capture (a particle-array reallocation) rather than the inventory's n_g. Attempt 4: the connected cathode ignited the channel (S 1.4e16 -> 7.3e16 /s in 0.39 us, the continuity cathode following I_d to 7 mA) with S unchecked by the falling inventory until S = 1.26 Q, the relaxation toward the negative fixed point emptied the channel in one 30 ns interval (5.5e19 -> 4.2e18), and the MCC then kept the trough density (S/(n_e n_g) x100 low at an unchanged T_e distribution) so the discharge did not recover when n_g refilled; the ignition gate stopped it at 0.75 us. The density is now a one-element device array read by mcc_kernel (warp_backend.set_neutral_scale copies into it), as the emission rate already was; the direct and graph paths are bitwise while n_g changes every interval (tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_neutral_inventory.py::test_cuda_graph_step_sees_every_neutral_density_update, which fails on the old backend). Affected runs: plume attempts 3-5 only (attempt 3's n_g stayed within 5.6-6.3e19; its cathode-coupling diagnosis stands). Unaffected: every v1.3 record (steady-state v2 base, seed-b, W x 0.7 - launched before the graph commit 112bb250) and the CPU/host-launch paths
neutrals_v2_0.ion_neutral: OFF (no CEX / elastic Xe+-Xe): the Miller et al. 2002 hash-bound table is the declared next sensitivity flag (review 4.1); the plume IEDF and j_i(theta) are therefore collisionless-ion development numbers (Duras et al. 2017: CEX shapes the far plume distributions)
neutrals_v2_0.recorded: neutral.* as v1.4; currents_a.plume_ionization_rate_per_s; cumulative ionizations_plume

thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.momentum_ledger: per series interval, axial: dP = impulse(E, B) + collisions + born + injected - exit - wall - anode (macro-weighted, both species); residual is round-off (tests); keys MOMENTUM_KEYS in cumulative
thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.thrust_momentum_flux: T_flux = sum over far-field crossings of m v_z W / dt per species minus the momentum brought in by the cathode; T_total = T_flux + cold gas, cold gas = Phi_effusion m (pi/4) v_bar (half-Maxwellian momentum flux through the aperture)
thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.thrust_momentum_balance: -F_on_thruster with F_on_thruster = (momentum deposited on the anode, wall and front face) - (field impulse on the plasma: E and B, the magnets are part of the thruster); closure = (T_flux - (-F_on_thruster)) normalised; the non-closing terms (stored momentum rate, collision momentum handed to the neutrals, far-field electrostatic force, born momentum) are reported
thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.electrostatic_force: independent field-side check: Maxwell stress T.n integrated over the plasma-side faces of the plasma cell mask touching each solid (anode, dielectric incl. the tangential-field pressure on the cone steps and the front-face ring, front-face conductor, far field); Newton's third law F_plasma + F_thruster + F_far = 0 holds to the first-order discretisation error of the one-sided boundary fields (test: 28 % -> 5.8 % -> 2.5 % at 0.25 / 0.125 / 0.0625 mm)
thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.far_field_histograms: ion current per steradian about the aperture centre j_i(theta), 90 bins over 0-90 deg; IEDF 256 bins to 1.5 U_a; side (cylinder) and plane current densities per species; all window accumulations
thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.derived: 95 % divergence half-angle from the theta histogram; IEDF mean and peak, peak - U_a (Koch et al. IEPC-2011-236: ion-energy peak ~ U_a - 15 V for the HEMP-T 3050 - the validation-v1 observable, reported as context, not validated at this closure); exit-plane axis potential (self-consistent); acceleration region = z where the axis potential has dropped 90 % and 10 % of the way from its maximum to the far plane; Isp = T_total / (m_dot g0); anode efficiency = T_total^2 / (2 m_dot U_a I_d)
thrust_and_plume_diagnostics_v2_0.claim_boundary: development numbers bound to the box size and the closure (Dirichlet far field, no CEX, volumetric cathode); Brandt et al. 2016 and Keller et al. 2015 (thrust 50-360 uN, Isp 230-860 s for the downscaled HEMPT family) are model-to-model / different-device context, never validation

gates_v2_0.inherited: peak-node Debye gate, grid-heating triad, omega_pe dt, Courant, Poisson residual contract, neutral inventory bounds - evaluated over the whole L-shaped domain
gates_v2_0.plume_boundary_gate: PlumeBoundaryGateConfig(max_charge_fraction, enforce_after_s, window_steps = 400000, min_accumulated_macro_particles_per_node = 64000) [v2.0.2, 2026-09-04]: at every series record the gate quantity is max over RESOLVED far-field nodes of |<n_i> - <n_e>| / <n_e,peak>, where <.> is the time average over the trailing window of at least window_steps ACCUMULATED steps, read from the SAME window accumulators that produce maps.npz and the frames (sum_t n_e, sum_t n_i on the far-field nodes, DiagnosticAccumulator / the Warp device sums d_n_e, d_n_i) at the series-record host sync - no per-step host sync is added; on the Warp backend the read is two node arrays per record next to the existing charge-map / potential / gate-moment reads. The Simulation keeps cumulative far-field totals that bridge the runner's accumulator resets (a reset increments the backend's diagnostic_generation and the last reading before it is carried; the runner resets right after a series record, so nothing is lost) and a ring of totals per record, so the window is the exact difference of two totals (the frame recorder's construction, frames.interval_maps). The denominator is the mean over the window's records of the instantaneous peak electron density. A far-field node is RESOLVED when its accumulated macro-particle weight over the window, (sum_t n_e + sum_t n_i) V_node / W (macro-particle-steps; = 2 x sample_count_e on a quasi-neutral node), is >= min_accumulated_macro_particles_per_node. The gate is enforced when armed (t >= enforce_after_s) AND the window holds >= window_steps accumulated steps; a violation stops the run fail-closed (PIC2DStabilityError 'plume-boundary gate'). The window history is not checkpointed: after a resume the statistic covers the accumulation since the resume and the gate is enforced again once the window is complete (0.6 us on the plume protocol; disclosed in the record via far_field_window_steps / far_field_window_complete / gate_armed / gate_enforced). Recorded per record: charge_fraction_of_peak (gate quantity), far_field_net_charge_density_max_per_m3, far_field_window_steps / _records / _start_step / _complete / _steps_required, far_field_resolved_nodes, min_accumulated_macro_particles_per_node, far_field_accumulated_macro_particles_max / _median, the unrestricted window statistic over ALL far-field nodes (charge_fraction_of_peak_window_raw, its node and accumulated weight), peak_electron_density_window_per_m3, and the v2.0.1 single-deposit statistic as the shot-noise witness (charge_fraction_of_peak_raw, far_field_raw_max_node, far_field_raw_max_macro_particles). Series arrays plume_far_field_window_steps, plume_charge_fraction_of_peak_window_raw, plume_peak_electron_density_window_per_m3, plume_far_field_accumulated_macro_particles_max; summary plume.charge_fraction_of_peak_window_raw_max, far_field_window_steps_final, far_field_resolved_nodes_final; log column q_far=<gate>(w<steps>/<resolved>n raw <window raw> dep <single deposit>). The far-field potential deviation from exit_v is recorded (Dirichlet: exactly 0). Rationale of the gate is unchanged: a sheath on the box boundary means the box is too small for the beam to leave quasi-neutrally (Brandt et al. 2016).

gates_v2_0.plume_boundary_gate_floor_and_window_jus: Window = 400000 accumulated steps = 0.6 us = the protocol's averaging window = 20 frames (the interval the attempt-6/7 diagnoses actually used: 0.030-0.035 max over the far-field nodes). Floor = 32 x 2000 = 64000 macro-particle-steps: an accumulated weight A counts particle-steps; a beam ion at the far plane (~15 km/s: attempt-7 flux-weighted <v_z> 14.8 km/s, IEDF 10 % quantile 13 km/s) stays on a 50 um node for tau = 50 um / (15 km/s x 1.5 ps) = 2000 steps (the ~10 series intervals per corner-node crossing in the attempt-6 log), so N_eff = A / (w tau) >= A / tau independent samples (bilinear weight w <= 1) and A >= 32 tau guarantees >= 32 independent beam-ion crossings (the peak-node Debye gate's 32-particle convention, relative shot noise <= 18 %) for every particle at least as fast as the beam; electrons (60x faster) only add samples; only the slow wide-angle ion wings (< 10 % of the far-field flux) are counted optimistically. Over the 400000-step window this is a mean occupancy of 0.16 macro-particles per node. Calibration on the attempt-6 and attempt-7 window maps (results-attempt6-gate-shot-noise / results-attempt7-wall-budget-no-plateau maps.npz, 400000 steps): 481 far-field nodes; accumulated weights 4.9e3 (r = 12 mm on the far plane) to 1.5e6 (r = 1 mm), corner node (0, 720) 3.3e4 / 4.1e4 (occupancy 0.08 / 0.10); a floor of 32 particle-steps resolves all 481 nodes (inert as a floor), 64000 resolves 77 (attempt 6) / 121 (attempt 7) of them - the far plane out to r = 3.9 / 6.7 mm plus the innermost side nodes - and reads max 0.0249 / 0.0339 of the peak at node (1, 720) (the unresolved corner node reads 0.0395 / 0.0346): the gate is live with a 7x margin to the 0.25 threshold instead of 0.000 (v2.0.1). A genuine sheath at 0.25 of the peak puts >= 0.73 macro-ions on the corner node and >= 4.4 on its neighbour at all times, i.e. is resolved everywhere but the corner. Shot-noise false-trip risk at the corner node under a 20000-step (one-frame) window would have been ~1e-5 per window (Poisson(1) >= 8 crossings) x ~300 windows per run - the reason for the 400000-step window rather than the frame cadence; at 400000 steps the same event needs 146 crossings against a mean of 20. Threshold (0.25) and arming time (2.4 us) unchanged.
gates_v2_0.plume_boundary_gate_history: v2.0 (attempts 3-6): single-deposit max |n_i - n_e| over the 481 far-field nodes / instantaneous peak n_e - a shot-noise extreme value; attempt 6 (PID 53824) ignited and was stopped at 2.466 us (66 ns after arming) by 0.66 macro-ions and no electrons on the axis corner node (0, 720) of the far plane (shape volume pi dr^2 dz / 6 = 6.5e-14 m^3: one macro-particle of W = 6e4 = 9.2e17 m^-3 = 0.39 of the 2.3e18 peak), reading 0.259 while the interval average was 0.03. v2.0.1 (45edd30e, attempt 7 PID 52176 and attempt 8 PID 51256 = resume of attempt 7): single-deposit statistic restricted to nodes holding >= 32 macro-particles in that deposit - at far-field densities (1e16-1e17 m^-3 x 6.5e-14-1e-11 m^3 / W = 0.01-20 macro-particles per node) no node ever reached the floor: 0 resolved nodes in all 4601 armed records of attempt 7, resolved statistic 0.000 throughout while the raw single-deposit statistic exceeded 0.25 in 0.8 % of the records (max 0.37) and the true 400000-step window average was 0.035 - the gate was INERT (could not fire), DISCLOSED here and in the plume protocol / README; attempts 7-8 keep the v2.0.1 configuration identity (the gate fields are part of config_sha256, so attempt 8's checkpoint cannot be resumed under v2.0.2; a fresh start from attempt 9 applies v2.0.2). v2.0.2 (this entry): window-averaged statistic from the diagnostic accumulators with an accumulated-weight floor; the single-deposit statistic stays recorded as the witness. Runner tooling in the same change: the nvidia-smi utilisation sampler moved to a background daemon thread at a configurable cadence (default 300 s; --gpu-sample-interval-seconds), the step loop reads a shared last value (attempt 7: 17 of 238 synchronous calls hit the 5 s timeout, 3.9 % of the wall budget); summary.gpu_utilisation_sampler records the cadence and outcome counts; the launch-time provenance line reports step_graph as 'lazy' until the first capture (it read false before).
gates_v2_0.peak_debye_gate_v2_0_3: PeakDebyeGateConfig(max_cells_per_debye = pi, min_macro_particles_at_peak = 32, dense_fraction = 0.5, window_steps = 400000, window_snapshot_steps = 40000, soft_cells_per_debye = 2.5) [v2.0.3, 2026-09-04, after plume attempt 8]: the GATED statistic is the interval-averaged peak. At every series record the Simulation reads the electron window sums over the WHOLE node map (sum_t n_e, sum_t w, sum_t w v_r, sum_t w v_theta, sum_t w v_z, sum_t w v^2 - the accumulators behind maps.npz and the frames; Warp: six node arrays at the record host sync next to the five single-step gate moments, no per-step sync), keeps cumulative totals that bridge the runner's 400000-step accumulator resets (carry on the backend's diagnostic_generation, as the v2.0.2 far-field window does) and a ring of cumulative snapshots every window_snapshot_steps accumulated steps (memory: window_steps / window_snapshot_steps + 2 full node-map sets, ~40 MB on the 90 x 720 channel grid, 12 snapshots), so the trailing window is an exact difference of two totals spanning window_steps .. window_steps + window_snapshot_steps accumulated steps (PeakDebyeWindow; window_peak_debye is the pure function). Peak = the densest plasma node whose MEAN OCCUPANCY over the window (sum_t w / steps) is >= min_macro_particles_at_peak macro-electrons (the v1.4 floor on the window mean; every channel peak node holds ~100-300 macro-electrons per step, so the floor only excludes the shot-noise axis nodes); <n_e> = sum_t n_e / steps; T_e = m_e (sum w v^2 / sum w - |sum w v / sum w|^2) / 3e = maps.npz t_e_ev at that node; gate quantity max(dr, dz) / lambda_D(<n_e>, T_e). HARD (fail-closed, PIC2DStabilityError 'peak-node Debye gate (window)'): > max_cells_per_debye = pi, the Birdsall-Langdon finite-grid-instability threshold of the momentum-conserving CIC scheme (Birdsall and Langdon 1985 ch. 8; Birdsall and Maron 1980; Ueda et al. 1994), enforced only when the window is complete (>= window_steps accumulated) AND a resolved node exists; the first 0.6 us after a fresh start or a resume are recorded, not gated (peak_node.window.window_complete / gate_enforced disclose it per record; the window history is not checkpointed). SOFT: soft_cells_per_debye = 2.5 (20 % under pi) is the declared resolution margin: recorded per record (peak_node.window.soft_exceeded, None while not enforced) and a PLATEAU PRECONDITION in the runner (evaluate_peak_debye_window -> plateau.peak_debye_soft_ok, summary.peak_node_debye.window), never a stop - a physically plateaued run between 2.5 and pi is recorded as 'plateau rule not declarable: resolution margin' and runs to its budget. The single-step sample (peak_node.cells_per_debye etc.) stays recorded as the shot-noise witness with gate_mode 'window' and gate_enforced false; series arrays peak_node_window_{cells_per_debye, n_e_peak_per_m3, t_e_peak_ev, window_steps, mean_macro_particles_at_peak, resolved_nodes, r_m, z_m}; status line peak_node.window; log column win=<value>(w<steps>[ n/e]). Configuration identity: the three window keys are emitted only in window mode, so every v1.4 / v2.0.0-v2.0.2 identity is unchanged (tests pin the v2.0.2 plume identities 1937f379.. / 4c969bff.. from the checked-in v2.0.3 protocol with the window keys stripped, and the v2.0.3 identities f7a4bedd.. / e1377abd..).
gates_v2_0.windowed_energy_residual_gate_v2_0_3: protocol stopping_rule.grid_heating_triad += {residual_window_steps: 400000, windowed_energy_residual_over_electrode_work_max: 0.05} [v2.0.3]: evaluate_triad (runner, every checkpoint) sums the interval energy-ledger residual and the interval electrode work over the records of the trailing residual_window_steps (records with step > last - window; complete when a record exists before the window) and forms the RESIDUAL POWER FRACTION residual / electrode work. ONE-SIDED: a positive residual is energy the scheme created (finite-grid heating); ratio >= 0.05 with the window complete stops the run (stop_reason grid_heating_triad_gate_stopped_run, hard_failures 'windowed energy residual / electrode work ... (finite-grid heating)'), enforced from the first complete window (no transit arming). The cumulative ratio energy_residual_over_electrode_work is RECORDED as the witness (cumulative_residual_is_witness_only = true), keeps its 10 % bound as a soft plateau precondition, and no longer stops the run; the soft check additionally requires the window ratio < 0.05. Recorded: windowed_energy_residual_over_electrode_work, _window_steps, _window_complete, _electrode_work_j, _j; thresholds carry both bounds. Without residual_window_steps the v1.4 cumulative hard member is unchanged (v1.4 / v2.0.0-v2.0.2 protocols). Calibration: (i) plume attempt 8 - per-0.4-us-window residual / electrode work -0.5 % (2.0-2.4 us) -> +2.4 (2.4-2.8) -> +5.8 (2.8-3.2) -> +11.3 -> +15.3 -> +23.5 -> +37.0 -> +54.8 % (4.8-5.0 us), residual power +45 -> +719 mW against 1.37-1.55 W of electrode power; the cumulative ratio was +8.6 % (bound 10 %) when the S-drift member stopped the run at 4.98 us and lagged the window ratio by ~1 us; this gate would have stopped it at ~3.2 us. (ii) the accepted channel-only plateau runs (pic2d_cft_steady_state_v2 results / results-seed-b / results-w-0.7): trailing-400000-step ratios at the checkpoints are NEGATIVE throughout - base -12.7 % (0-0.6 us) -> -11.8 -> -10.0 -> -8.9 -> -7.2 -> -6.0 -> -4.7 -> -3.6 -> -2.7 -> -1.7 -> -1.0 -> -0.2 % (6.6-7.2 us), max +0.37 %; seed-b -12.8 % -> -1.5 %; W x 0.7 -12.7 % -> -4.2 % - so the one-sided 5 % bound is silent on every accepted run, while a two-sided 5 % bound would have stopped all three before 4 us (test test_windowed_residual_gate_never_fires_on_the_accepted_channel_only_plateau reads the base series.npz). The sign convention: residual = dE_total - accounted sources; the accepted runs' negative residual is the scheme's numerical cooling / unaccounted loss during the seed dump decaying toward zero at the plateau, the plume runs' positive residual is grid heating.
gates_v2_0.gate_recalibration_history_v2_0_3: Why v2.0.3 (2026-09-04 11:38 AEST, attempt 8 = resume of attempt 7, PID 51256, stopped at 3.32 M steps / 4.98 us / 1.61 transits by the S-drift triad member at +0.253): the discharge kept densifying under the v1.4 single-step peak-Debye gate at 4.5 (reading 3.64 -> 3.75, max 4.28 on a transient argmax) and the cumulative residual bound 0.10 (reading +0.0857). The energy ledger's residual per 0.4 us segment changed sign at 2.0-2.4 us, exactly when the window-averaged peak Delta/lambda_D crossed ~3.2 (2.96 -> 3.23 -> 3.37 -> 3.58 -> 3.66-3.75), i.e. the CIC threshold pi; 47 % of the last segment's energy budget was grid heating (residual +646 mW vs electrode +1373 mW, accounted physical sources -615 mW). The accepted channel-only base plateau (24ab82f4, results/, 3.2 transits) sat at 3.17 at its peak (1.64e18 m^-3, T_e 7.4 eV, node (14, 286) on the 60 x 480 grid) with the residual closing to +0.4 %: the two runs bracket the heating onset at Delta/lambda_D ~ 3.2, the declared 4.5 was not protective, and the base plateau itself sits ON the threshold (its convergence is tested by pic2d_cft_steady_state_v4 at 33.3 um / 1.4 ps). Thresholds: hard pi (the threshold itself; a run above it IS heating), soft 2.5 = 20 % margin (Delta <= 32.4 um at the attempt-8 peak 3.69e18 / 11.1 eV; the 33.3 um grid gives 2.11 at the base peak 1.64e18 / 7.4 eV); residual power 5 % = the attempt-8 value of the 2.8-3.2 us window (the first clearly heating window) and 12x the accepted plateau's largest positive window value; cumulative ratio demoted to a witness because its whole-history denominator lags the onset by ~1 us. Not changed: omega_pe dt 0.2, Courant, Poisson contract, drift members (S, T_e,dense, omega_pe dt; soft 0.05 / hard 0.25 after one transit), plume boundary gate v2.0.2, neutral bounds. Applies to fresh starts (the window keys are in config_sha256): plume attempt 9+, plume v2.1, and the channel-only refinement campaign pic2d_cft_steady_state_v4.

frame_recorder_v2_0.purpose: time-series video of the whole run (maps evolving), not only the window-averaged final maps; a diagnostics artefact with no effect on the dynamics (nothing added to the step kernels)
frame_recorder_v2_0.config: numerics.frame_recorder = {cadence_steps, precision} in the protocol (absent = OFF, the v1.x behaviour); the plume development run declares cadence 20000 steps = 30 ns at dt 1.5 ps, float32
frame_recorder_v2_0.content: per frame, over the FULL domain: exact interval averages of n_e, n_i, phi, T_e (from the accumulated moments, drift-corrected), ionisation rate and the electron sample counts (node maps); wall electron/ion flux, exit and side (far-field) current-density profiles, j_i(theta) and the IEDF of the interval; the instantaneous dielectric surface charge at the frame end; the scalar series record at the frame end (t, I_d, I_beam, S, N_e, N_i, n_g, thrust flux/balance/total, closure, cathode current, mean T_e)
frame_recorder_v2_0.method: the window accumulators are additive sums reset at window boundaries; a frame is the difference of two cumulative snapshots divided through by DiagnosticAccumulator.to_arrays, so it is the exact average over (a, b] with T_e from the interval's own moments (differencing the finished maps could not give T_e). Alignment contract, fail-closed at start: cadence is a multiple of device_sync_steps and divides checkpoint_every_steps and averaging_window_steps, so every checkpoint and window reset is a frame boundary
frame_recorder_v2_0.storage: frames/frame-NNNNNN.npz, one compressed file per frame written atomically (temp + replace) BEFORE the checkpoint that follows it; on resume/finalize the frames ending after the checkpoint step are removed (a crash between a frame and its checkpoint cannot duplicate or drop a frame); the manifest (count, bytes, step range, SHA-256 over the sorted per-file digests, config) is hash-bound in summary.json artifacts.frames; bitwise deterministic for the same run (test: byte-identical frames from a fresh run; frames of the first session untouched by the resume)
frame_recorder_v2_0.size: 241 x 721 nodes x float32 x 7 arrays = 4.9 MB/frame uncompressed (measured 7:1 zip on the tiny fixture; expect 2-4:1 on the real grid); 100-140 frames in the 4 h budget = 0.5-0.7 GB, 257 frames (7.7 us) = 1.26 GB uncompressed: inside the 1-2 GB envelope with no spatial downsampling; the HTML player downsamples 2x (block mean, counts summed) itself
frame_recorder_v2_0.renderer: modern/visualization/render_pic2d_video.py: (a) one MP4 per map (H.264 yuv420p, CRF 18) through imageio_ffmpeg if importable (installed in .venv-sota only), else the ffmpeg executable on PATH (raw RGB pipe), else an animated GIF through Pillow - the backend used is reported; frames carry the map (nearest upscale), the plasma-mask outline (thruster body), cusp planes, a fixed colour bar and a synchronised strip of I_d / I_beam / N_e / n_g / T with a cursor; (b) pic2d-<run>-timeseries.html: offline player with the frames embedded as 2x-downsampled palette PNGs (float32 -> 254 colour indices + body + mask), scrubber / play / speed / map selector / keyboard arrows, body outline and cusp planes drawn, synchronised time series under the map, hash-bound to the frames manifest and the protocol
frame_recorder_v2_0.colour_scale: fixed across ALL frames so the eye sees evolution, not autoscaling: log10 with a floor of max/10^4 for n_e and n_i (maximum over the unmasked plasma nodes of all frames); full range for phi (diverging palette); 0 to the 99.5th percentile for T_e; cells with fewer than N = 20 electron samples in the interval are grey (the sampling mask of the dashboards), non-plasma nodes dark
frame_recorder_v2_0.ionisation_panel_v0_2: a single 30 ns frame of the ionisation map is shot noise by construction (map = events W / (V_node dt) with events the bilinear-deposited macro-ionisation weight; attempt 6: ~73 % of electron-resolved nodes hold zero events per frame, one event on an axis node ~3e25 m^-3 s^-1 set the per-frame top). The renderer shows a CAUSAL rolling window of K frames (windowed events = trailing sum, partial over the first K-1 frames; windowed rate = windowed events W / (V_node windowed time) = the time-weighted mean of the frame rates, integrating exactly to the window's mean S), greys out nodes with fewer than 20 windowed macro-ionisation events (the dashboards' ionisation-event mask, 'unresolved', never zero), and fixes the log10 scale between the 0.5th and 99.5th percentile of the resolved windowed values over the whole run (not the maximum). K defaults to the smallest window whose median electron-resolved node carrying >= 1 event weight holds >= 10 events (choose_window); window, mask threshold, scale basis and the per-frame resolved share of S are written into the legend and the player caption; no spatial smoothing. Attempt 6: K = 11 (330 ns), scale 1.6e23-2.9e24, resolved nodes carry 67 % of S on average (77 % at the end)
frame_recorder_v2_0.tests: tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_frames.py (3): config/alignment contract and the real protocol's size envelope; exact interval algebra on a synthetic accumulator (maps, fluxes, histograms to 1e-9, T_e to 1e-6); runner cadence/shapes/scalars, window-mean consistency, manifest, stray-frame removal on resume, contiguity, first-session frames untouched, byte-identical fresh run, OFF by default. tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_video_renderer.py (13): palette mapping (lo/mid/hi, zero/NaN on log, sample mask, body precedence, clipping), fixed scales (mask-aware maximum), block downsampling, outline, GIF/MP4 writers, deterministic render_run on a tiny run with a validated hash-bound payload and CLI; ionisation panel: events reproduce the recorded counts and the domain integral, causal trailing sums, Poisson frames -> windowed rate converges to the true rate (5 sigma per node, RMS ~ 1/sqrt(K)) and equals the time-weighted mean, windowed rate integrates to the window's mean S, a single-event axis node is masked as unresolved and does not set the scale top (the pre-v0.2 scale did), choose_window is the smallest K meeting the median target, robust percentile scale and its degenerate fall-backs, legend / payload declarations, payload validation of the window and mask blocks, suffix and CLI options

performance_v2_0_5.status: implemented 2026-09-04 (code + tests commit f80c6441 = the verified a156fd84 rebased onto ee35bc84 with identical file contents; docs/spec follow); verified on the Lambda H100 as an extra CUDA-MPS client next to four preregistered runs (Class A / A-prime protocol of docs/pic2d-performance-audit.md section 9, budget-scaled: 40 000-step same-seed replays from the seed instead of 100 000, a 6 000-step resume of an anchored production checkpoint instead of 400 000 - the running preregistered jobs (mini-sweep at 291a9227, ext-val v0 at 3dc12cf6, v5 launch 2 at 351257f2) keep the code they were sealed with; a new preregistration names the code commit and cites this block)
what_changed: born ledger (audit item k): mcc_kernel forms ke_born = KE(ion Maxwellian draw, m_i W) and pz_born = m_i W v_z,ion + m_e W v_z,secondary per ionising electron and tile-reduces them into STATS_KE_BORN / STATS_PZ_BORN with its other seven tallies; the three 4096-thread strided sums (energy_sum_kernel, 2 x momentum_sum_kernel) and three single-thread deferred_add_kernel launches after the spawn are gone (they were 1.1-1.2 ms of the 3.31 ms solo channel-33 step, 2.0 ms of the 7.2 ms plume-50 step)

born deposits fused into spawn_kernel: the born ion's bilinear weights go into the frozen ion charge accumulator (int64 2^-40 fixed point, order independent -> acc_i bitwise the former separate deposit_fixed over born_r/born_z/born_flag) and, when accumulating, into the ionisation-rate window map; deposit_unit_kernel, deferred_add_kernel and the born_* scratch arrays are removed (per step: -5 launches, -5 capacity-sized flag passes)

window diagnostics off the critical path (audit item f2): inside the captured step the branch that reads only the pre-push state (d_n_e / d_n_i from this step's deposits, the electron moment deposition) is forked onto WarpBackend.side_stream after the charge deposits (Stream.wait_stream fork event) and joined before the push (join event), so its 20 float64 atomics per electron overlap the latency-bound block-Thomas chain; CUDA-graph fork/join through events IS graph-capturable in Warp 1.14 (wp.Stream, wp.Event, ScopedStream(sync_enter=False); 3 captures per particle-array allocation at K = 1, 6 at K > 1: the graph key gains the moments flag). The direct (non-graph) path and the CPU device launch the same kernels inline; d_phi += phi stays after the solve

electron-moment sampling (audit item f1): PIC2DConfig.moment_sample_interval K deposits the moments (sum w, sum w v_r/v_theta/v_z, sum w v^2) every K-th ACCUMULATED step on both backends, phase anchored on the window's accumulated-step count (diag_steps % K == 0; a window reset restarts it); moment_samples counts the samples and travels with the sums (DiagnosticAccumulator.raw_sums/from_sums, diagnostic_sums, peak_window_sums, the frame recorder's interval differences; snapshots without the count fall back to one sample per step). The per-step accumulators (n_e, n_i, phi, ionisation, wall / exit / side fluxes, theta / IEDF histograms) are untouched
performance_v2_0_5.why_physics_bitwise: nothing that feeds back on the dynamics changed: the particle push, the fixed-point charge deposition (the fused born deposit adds the same int64 quanta at the same positions - integer addition is order independent), the Poisson solve, the MCC draws (same RNG stream, same per-particle branch) and the injection are byte-identical kernels or byte-identical arithmetic; the fork only reorders diagnostic launches whose outputs no physics kernel reads before the join. The two ledger scalars ke_born_ions_j and pz_born change in summation order only (per-block tile sums + one atomic per block instead of 4096 strided partials + a serial add): declared tolerance <= 1e-12 relative - the same class as the recorded float-atomic diagnostics (MPS replay criterion). Overflow corner: the old sums counted only spawned births, the new tallies every ionisation event; a spawn overflow raises at the next sync in both codes, so no recorded run can differ
performance_v2_0_5.k_semantics: the moment maps are ratios of sums over the SAME sampled steps (T_e = m_e (sum w v^2 / sum w - |sum w v / sum w|^2) / 3e, drift = sum w v / sum w): unbiased time averages over the sampled steps, no normalisation needed; the peak-Debye window's occupancy floor reads sum w / moment_samples (mean macro-electrons per node over the samples, = the v2.0.3 quantity at K = 1) and its density sum_t n_e / steps is per-step and K-independent, so n_e_peak, the far-field gate, n_e / n_i / phi maps and every flux are bitwise the K = 1 values; only T_e-derived quantities (t_e_ev, cells_per_debye, sample_count_e = the number of particle-samples) become sampled estimators. Because an electron stays on a 33 um node for ~24 steps at 1.4 ps, consecutive steps are near-duplicate samples and K = 5 loses almost no independent information (measured below). d_w is kept: it equals d_n_e only at K = 1; under sampling it is the moments' own denominator. K must divide device_sync_steps (runner rule) so every frame / window / checkpoint boundary holds a whole number of samples; window gate records carry window_moment_samples only when K != 1 (K = 1 records keep the v2.0.3 layout byte for byte). Recommended production value K = 5 (200 % 5 == 0); K = 1 stays available and is the default
performance_v2_0_5.identity_decision: K = 1: PIC2DConfig.to_dict is unchanged, every v2.0.x config_sha256 pin (v4 f10772b2..., v5, mini-sweep, ext-val) holds, so the performance block does NOT enter the identity when it is absent or 1 - the code change is invisible to the configuration contract (only the code identity of a preregistration names it). K != 1: moment_sample_interval is written into to_dict and therefore into config_sha256, because the window statistics (T_e maps, the gated cells_per_debye, sample counts) become sampled estimators - a diagnostics-contract change that must not be silent
